description: Real open-source GitHub Issue/PR benchmark (12 Fix + 8 Review) from pluggy, packaging, and click.

fix_tasks.title: Fix declined entry point distribution tracking
fix_tasks.problem_statement: In `PluginManager.load_setuptools_entrypoints`, when `self.register(plugin, name=ep.name)` returns `None` (for example because registration was declined/ignored), the method still records `self._name2dist[ep.name] = dist` and increments `count`. Also if `register()` returns a canonical plugin name, `_name2dist` should be keyed by the returned plugin name rather than assuming `ep.name`. Fix `load_setuptools_entrypoints` so declined registrations are neither tracked in `_name2dist` nor counted in the returned plugin count.

fix_tasks.title: Raise TypeError/ValueError from unregister() instead of assert (#762)
fix_tasks.problem_statement: `PluginManager.unregister(plugin=None, name=None)` uses `assert` to check that at least one of `name` or `plugin` is provided and that the given `plugin` is registered. Under `python -O`, `assert` statements are stripped, causing `unregister()` with no arguments to return `None` and `unregister(unregistered_plugin)` to return the plugin instead of raising an error. Replace these assertions with explicit runtime checks: raise `TypeError` when neither `name` nor `plugin` is specified, and raise `ValueError` when `plugin` is given without `name` and is not registered.

fix_tasks.title: Raise ValueError when unregister's plugin and name disagree
fix_tasks.problem_statement: The docstring of `PluginManager.unregister(plugin=None, name=None)` states that if both `plugin` and `name` are specified, they must agree. Currently, `unregister()` looks up hook callers by `plugin` but removes the registry entry by `name`, so passing a `plugin` and `name` that refer to different plugins corrupts the registry by mutating both plugins. Validate both directions before mutating any state and raise `ValueError` when `plugin` and `name` disagree.

fix_tasks.title: Skip registered entrypoint plugins without checking truthiness
fix_tasks.problem_statement: In `PluginManager.load_setuptools_entrypoints`, checking whether an entry point is already registered uses `or self.get_plugin(ep.name)`. If a registered plugin object is falsy (e.g., implements `__bool__` returning `False` or `__len__` returning `0`), `self.get_plugin(ep.name)` evaluates to falsy and the entry point is loaded and registered again, causing an error or duplicate load. Check plugin existence without evaluating the plugin's truthiness (e.g., `has_plugin`).

fix_tasks.title: Fix subset_hook_caller getting confused by specname
fix_tasks.problem_statement: `PluginManager.subset_hook_caller(name, remove_plugins)` currently filters `remove_plugins` using `hasattr(plug, name)`. However, when a plugin defines a hook implementation using `@hookimpl(specname=...)`, its attribute name on the plugin does not match the hook `name`, so `subset_hook_caller` fails to exclude that plugin. Fix `subset_hook_caller` so plugins in `remove_plugins` are properly matched against the hook's registered hookimpls regardless of `specname`.

fix_tasks.title: Parse === followed by a spaced specifier in Requirement (#1500/#1531)
fix_tasks.problem_statement: Parsing a requirement that contains an arbitrary equality specifier (`===`) followed by a comma and a spaced specifier (such as `foo === 1.0, != 2.0`) fails in `packaging._parser` because `_try_parse_specifier_set` skips any specifier list containing `===`, falling back to the token loop where the `===` token consumes too much. Fix requirement specifier parsing so `===` followed by additional comma-separated specifiers parses cleanly into a `SpecifierSet`.

fix_tasks.title: Report self-inclusion for unnormalized spellings in dependency-groups (#1519)
fix_tasks.problem_statement: In `packaging.dependency_groups.DependencyGroupResolver._validate`, the included group name is normalized before checking for cycles against the include stack, but the raw unnormalized `item.include_group` is passed to `CyclicDependencyGroup`. Because `CyclicDependencyGroup` checks `include_group == group` (where `group` is already normalized), a self-include using an unnormalized spelling (like `'A'` inside group `'a'`, or `'A_B'` inside `'a.b'`) produces a misleading two-group cycle message instead of a self-inclusion message. Pass the normalized `include_group` when constructing `CyclicDependencyGroup`.

fix_tasks.title: Reject non-ASCII LicenseRefs before normalization (#1481)
fix_tasks.problem_statement: In `packaging.licenses.canonicalize_license_expression`, custom `LicenseRef-...` identifiers are lowercased and normalized before validation, which can allow non-ASCII characters (for instance Unicode characters whose lowercase form interacts unexpectedly) to slip past or raise an inconsistent error. Reject any `LicenseRef-` token that is not ASCII by raising `InvalidLicenseExpression` before normalizing it.

fix_tasks.title: Fix show_envvar output for a sequence or an empty envvar
fix_tasks.problem_statement: In `click.Option`, when `show_envvar=True`: (1) `get_error_hint()` checks `self.envvar is not None` and formats `f" (env var: '{self.envvar}')"`, which breaks when `envvar` is a sequence of names (rendering a Python list repr) or an empty string/sequence (rendering an empty hint). Format each envvar name quoted and comma-separated, and omit the hint when `envvar` is empty. (2) In `get_help_extra()` / help display, also handle empty `envvar` (such as `""` or `[]`) cleanly instead of only checking `is None`.

fix_tasks.title: Fix copy, deepcopy and pickle of Sentinel members
fix_tasks.problem_statement: `click._utils.Sentinel` (and its singleton member `UNSET`) fails or loses singleton identity when copied with `copy.copy()`, `copy.deepcopy()`, or serialized/deserialized with `pickle.dumps()`/`pickle.loads()`. Implement `__copy__`, `__deepcopy__`, and `__reduce_ex__` on `Sentinel` so copying returns the exact same singleton member and unpickling resolves back to `getattr(Sentinel, name)`.

fix_tasks.title: Validate style() color arguments and fix explicit black/0 color
fix_tasks.problem_statement: In `click.termui._interpret_color` (used by `click.style()`), color validation has several bugs: (1) `bool` values (`True`/`False`) pass `isinstance(color, int)` and silently render as palette indices 1 and 0; (2) out-of-range integer palette indices (<0 or >255) and invalid RGB tuples (wrong length, bool elements, or values outside 0..255) are not rejected with `TypeError`/`ValueError`; (3) passing explicit color `0` (palette index 0 / black) in `style(fg=0)` or `style(bg=0)` is dropped if truthiness (`if fg:`) is checked instead of `is not None`. Fix color validation and handling of explicit `0` color values in `termui.py`.

fix_tasks.title: Strip ANSI from confirm() and prompt() when stream does not support them (#3572)
fix_tasks.problem_statement: When `click.prompt()` or `click.confirm()` passes a styled prompt string (containing ANSI escape codes) to the underlying prompt function (`input` via `_readline_prompt`), ANSI escape sequences are emitted raw even when the destination stream (`stdout` or `stderr`) does not support ANSI colors (e.g., redirected/non-TTY streams or `color=False` / `NO_COLOR`). Update prompt handling in `src/click/termui.py` so ANSI codes are stripped when the destination stream does not support ANSI.

review_tasks.title: feat: expose syntax error details on InvalidRequirement and InvalidMarker (#1547)

ground_truth.issue: In `InvalidMarker.__init__` and `InvalidRequirement.__init__`, calling `str(self)` eagerly inside `__init__` breaks subclasses or callers passing arguments that cannot be formatted during initialization (and adds unnecessary eager formatting work); `self.message` should be computed lazily (e.g. via `cached_property`) when `message is None`.

review_tasks.title: Allow creating a SpecifierSet from a list of specifiers (#777)

ground_truth.issue: When `SpecifierSet` receives a non-string iterable, it assigns `frozenset(specifiers)` directly without validating or parsing elements, so passing a list of plain strings (e.g. `SpecifierSet(['>=1.0'])`) or invalid element types silently stores raw strings and later breaks `SpecifierSet` operations instead of parsing `str` elements into `Specifier` objects or raising `TypeError`.

review_tasks.title: Rework the parser with context-sensitive tokenisation

ground_truth.issue: Recursive parsing of parenthesized marker groups (`_parse_marker` / `_parse_marker_atom`) has no nesting depth limit, so deeply nested parentheses exhaust Python's recursion limit and leak an unhandled `RecursionError` instead of raising a parser/syntax error (`InvalidMarker`).

When appending the deprecated label to `help` (when `help` is empty vs non-empty), the refactored formatting introduces leading/extra whitespace or misformats the deprecated label when `help` is empty or `None`.

In `Argument.make_metavar`, when `not self.required` and `var` is already wrapped in square brackets by types like `Choice` or `DateTime` (e.g. `[a|b]`), wrapping it again with `f'[{var}]'` produces double-bracketed output like `[[a|b]]`.

In `_make_default_short_help`, edge cases in abbreviation/period detection, `\b` marker handling, or truncation length calculation cause incorrect short-help truncation (e.g. treating abbreviations like 'e.g.'/'vs.' as sentence endings, or miscomputing remaining length / empty text after `\b`).

`version_option` assumes the detected top-level module name (from frame inspection) matches the installed distribution name passed to `importlib.metadata.version()`, failing whenever the import/module name differs from the distribution package name (e.g. `PIL` vs `Pillow`, or packages with different top-level module names).
Changing `PluginManager.register(None)` to raise `TypeError` is a breaking backwards-compatibility regression for downstream callers that pass `None` expecting a no-op (`return None`).
